newsitem.title: USA: Home Depot post record earnings, see stronger growth target.
newsitem.headline: Home Depot post record earnings, see stronger growth target.

text.p: Home Depot Inc., the nation's largest home improvement retailer, reported record earnings for the latest quarter Tuesday and boosted its long-term earnings growth target.

The company said it earned $251.1 million, or 52 cents a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Feb. 2 compared with year-earlier earnings of $185.3 million, or 39 cents a share. Sales jumped 32 percent to $5 billion from $3.8 billion.
For the year, Home Depot said it earned $937.8 million, or $1.94 a share, on sales of $19.5 billion against year earlier profits of $731.5 million, or $1.54 a share, on sales of $15.4 billion.
"They've had a good year. And the outlook for next year is quite strong. They had some impressive results," said Donald Spindel, an analyst at A.G. Edwards & Co.
"They continue to gain market share. A lot of the growth they are seeing is from their aggressive new store expansion. But their existing stores continue to make a nice contribution," he said.

Home Depot President Arthur Blank said the company now sees earnings per share growth of 23 percent to 25 percent annually over the next two to three years, up from a previous target of 20 percent to 25 percent.
In a conference call, he attributed the more optimistic outlook to a lengthy list of improvements, from enhanced customer service to the opening of a new distribution centre in Savannah, Ga.
"We are very hopeful that for the next two to three years, as we look out, that the annual earnings per share growth for the company will be in the range of 23-25 percent," Blank said.
The quarterly earnings were better than expected, and Home Depot's stock jumped $2.375 to $54.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Home Depot attributed the unexpectedly good results to the strength of its underlying business and consolidation in the retail home improvement industry, which combined to raise its 1996 market share to 14 percent from 12 percent.

Blank also said Home Depot would have three new growth initiatives in place by mid-year that would seek to improve sales from professional contractors, strike a more effective product mix and better utilize store space.
The company expects to spend $1.7 billion in 1997 to fund the addition of 111 new stores.

According to Blank, Home Depot will continue to use expansion as its main growth engine and wants to double its current number of stores over the next four years. That scale of expansion, he said, would reflect a continuation of its current 21 to 22 percent annual rate of store growth.

Home Depot said it continued to expand, adding 33 new stores and relocating two stores in the fourth quarter, bringing the total to 512 stores, including 483 Home Depot stores and 5 EXPO Design Centres in the United States and 24 Home Depot stores in Canada.
